To improve the previous baseline, I will replace the independent token mapping with a context-aware tri-gram lookup table. Text normalization in Russian heavily depends on syntactic neighbors (e.g., prepositions governing case, numerical classifiers), so incorporating immediate left/right tokens into the lookup key will capture these dependencies without requiring a heavy neural network. I will also enforce a sentence-wise train/validation split to prevent information leakage from overlapping sentence contexts, and use fully vectorized pandas operations to ensure rapid evaluation and prediction.

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import re
import os
import warnings

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

TRAIN_PATH = "./input/ru_train.csv"
TEST_PATH = "./input/ru_test_2.csv"
SUBMISSION_DIR = "./submission"
SUBMISSION_PATH = os.path.join(SUBMISSION_DIR, "submission.csv")
VALIDATION_SPLIT = 0.1
RANDOM_SEED = 42

os.makedirs(SUBMISSION_DIR, exist_ok=True)

print("Loading data...")
try:
    train_df = pd.read_csv(TRAIN_PATH, encoding="utf-8-sig")
except Exception:
    train_df = pd.read_csv(TRAIN_PATH)

try:
    test_df = pd.read_csv(TEST_PATH, encoding="utf-8-sig")
except Exception:
    test_df = pd.read_csv(TEST_PATH)

def clean_text(text):
    if pd.isna(text): return ""
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", str(text).strip())

print("Cleaning text...")
train_df["b_c"] = train_df["before"].apply(clean_text)
train_df["a_c"] = train_df["after"].apply(clean_text)
test_df["b_c"] = test_df["before"].apply(clean_text)

print("Splitting data (sentence-wise to prevent leakage)...")
rng = np.random.default_rng(RANDOM_SEED)
sent_ids = train_df["sentence_id"].unique()
rng.shuffle(sent_ids)
n_val = int(len(sent_ids) * VALIDATION_SPLIT)
val_sent_ids = set(sent_ids[:n_val])
train_mask = ~train_df["sentence_id"].isin(val_sent_ids)
train_only_df = train_df[train_mask].copy()
val_df = train_df[~train_mask].copy()

def add_context(df):
    df = df.copy().sort_values(["sentence_id", "token_id"]).reset_index(drop=True)
    df["prev_b"] = df.groupby("sentence_id")["b_c"].shift(1).fillna("<PAD>")
    df["next_b"] = df.groupby("sentence_id")["b_c"].shift(-1).fillna("<PAD>")
    df["uni_key"] = df["b_c"]
    df["tri_key"] = df["prev_b"] + "|||" + df["b_c"] + "|||" + df["next_b"]
    return df

print("Adding context features...")
train_only_df = add_context(train_only_df)
val_df = add_context(val_df)
test_df = add_context(test_df)

print("Building frequency maps...")
# Most frequent normalization for each context window
tri_map = train_only_df.groupby("tri_key")["a_c"].apply(lambda x: x.value_counts().index[0]).to_dict()
uni_map = train_only_df.groupby("uni_key")["a_c"].apply(lambda x: x.value_counts().index[0]).to_dict()

print("Validating...")
tri_preds = val_df["tri_key"].map(tri_map)
mask_tri = tri_preds.notna()
uni_preds = val_df["uni_key"].map(uni_map)
mask_uni = uni_preds.notna() & ~mask_tri
val_preds = tri_preds.fillna(uni_preds).fillna(val_df["b_c"])

accuracy = (val_preds == val_df["a_c"]).mean()
print(f"Validation Accuracy: {accuracy:.6f}")

print("Generating test predictions...")
test_tri_preds = test_df["tri_key"].map(tri_map)
mask_tri_t = test_tri_preds.notna()
test_uni_preds = test_df["uni_key"].map(uni_map)
mask_uni_t = test_uni_preds.notna() & ~mask_tri_t
